turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, I'm here because I keep getting these thoughts. I manage IT systems for work, and I just keep having this fear that if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, someone could get hurt or lose everything. And... even though part of me knows it’s irrational, it hits me like I’m personally responsible. I just can’t seem to move on from it.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes persistent, intrusive thoughts about causing severe harm through minor oversight, which they recognize as irrational but feel personally responsible for and unable to dismiss.

turns.doctor_question: When these thoughts hit, do you find yourself repeatedly checking things to feel sure nothing was missed?
turns.patient_response:
Yes, I do. All the time, honestly. I’ll go back and reread deployment plans, audit logs... even physical things like door locks, or old messages. I just check them over and over. 

Sometimes I find myself counting through the steps in my head until it finally feels safe. It gets so bad that I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. I just... if I try to walk away or stop before checking it all feels complete, I start to panic. So I just keep doing it.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive checking behaviors (audit logs, door locks, messages) and mental rituals (counting steps) to relieve panic until it feels safe.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that these thoughts and the checking you do are excessive or unreasonable?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. I mean... logically, I know it is. Spending hours at the office just rereading the same logs is definitely excessive. 

Like I said earlier, a part of me knows it's irrational. But... when I'm actually in the middle of it, it doesn't feel unreasonable at all. It feels completely necessary. It feels like if I don't do it, something terrible is going to happen and it will be my fault. So, yes, my logical brain knows it's way too much, but... I just can't seem to stop.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes intrusive, irrational thoughts that if they do not check, something terrible will happen and be their fault.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient reports spending hours rereading the same logs as an excessive checking behavior they feel compelled to do and cannot stop.

turns.doctor_question: Do these thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted to you?
turns.patient_response: Yes, very much so. Like I mentioned when I first sat down, I just keep getting these thoughts about missing a setting or an access rule, and someone getting hurt or losing everything because of it. I don't want to think about it. It just pops into my head and... hits me with this intense feeling that I'm personally responsible. I definitely don't want the thoughts, but I just can't seem to move on from them once they start.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly confirms having recurrent, unwanted thoughts popping into their head that they cannot move on from, fulfilling criteria for obsessions.

turns.doctor_question: When the fear is strongest, do you still believe there’s a real chance that missing one detail will cause serious harm?
turns.patient_response: Yes, absolutely. Even though I know logically it's excessive, in those moments... the fear is completely real. I genuinely believe that if I miss one small detail in a deployment plan or an access rule, the entire system could be compromised, and it would be a disaster. I feel like it really will happen, and it will be entirely my fault.

turns.doctor_question: When the fear is strongest, do you still recognize that your mind may be exaggerating the danger?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. When I'm in the middle of it, when that panic really hits... I don't think I'm exaggerating at all. It feels completely real. Like, I can't step back and say, "Oh, this is just my mind playing tricks on me." I'm just entirely convinced that the danger is right there, and I have to fix it or everything falls apart.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of those panic moments, do you believe the fear is probably not true?
turns.patient_response: Honestly, even when I'm not actively panicking, I still think there's a real chance something bad could happen. I mean, maybe I can see that the reaction is a bit much, but the core fear... I don't really ever think it's completely untrue. The risk always feels like it's there.
